assessment: Explicit source-path review for the dependency upgrade, retaining the original 2026-11-29 expiry and managed-default-server-DTLS scope. mediasoup 0.29.0 still creates an in-process Rust thread and directly calls mediasoup_worker_run; worker/utils.rs is unchanged from 0.27.0. The 0.19.0 DTLS source delta changes timer labels, signed timestamps and application-data receive timestamps while retaining OpenSSL SSL/BIO calls. The maintained authenticated-close, fingerprint and SRTP validation patches remain present. First-party production changes replace deprecated atomic calls and widen configuration inputs/saturate worker estimates at the existing application bitrate boundary; they introduce no subprocess, dynamic-loader, iconv or gconv call. The authenticated native inventory updates libuv and unordered_dense while using authenticated static OpenSSL 4.0.3, retaining no-module/no-engine options, and binding the updated checksum-verifying installer. The Cargo dependency graph and all source identities are rebound to the reviewed upgrade; optional load-test clients are not in the production image. The built-in files/dns NSS and restricted loader profile are unchanged. This assessment covers the intended production execution path, not every unused dependency API, engine-provided init, administrator-selected programs or arbitrary post-deployment mutation. Actual archive/final-binary identities, runtime restrictions and image findings remain independently enforced; changed source or profile bytes require fresh review. The OpenSSL 4 compatibility change replaces mutation of a borrowed X509 subject with an explicitly owned X509_NAME, copies it into subject and issuer, and frees it on success and failure. It does not add runtime module, engine, dynamic-library, command or subprocess loading; certificate subject/issuer equality and the self signature have explicit native regression coverage. Existing static archive, runtime loader, exact source and final-artifact proof requirements remain mandatory. Additional native dependency review on 2026-10-05 upgrades Abseil to 20260817.0 and FlatBuffers to the upstream 25.12.19-2026-02-06-03fffb2 release. Meson overlays retain authenticated wrapdb provenance and adjust only version/source-file lists to match those releases; complete archive/tree deviation checks pass. Planus 1.3.0 generates Rust bindings through its explicit typed API, and mediasoup async-channel/async-lock/fastrand/futures-lite/thiserror declarations move to current compatible releases. These source/build changes add no production process spawning, dynamic-library loading or locale conversion entry point. Previously reviewed static OpenSSL4.0.3 DTLS behavior, runtime profile, scope and expiry are retained. AWS-LC native dependency review on 2026-10-05 replaces the aws-lc-sys 0.45.0 wrapper's unused bundled 5.7.0 implementation with authenticated AWS-LC 5.11.0 release fa9bc8d6f7cfb2cf849b247fb06bbbfc41ecc9d6 through its supported system mode, retaining version checks. The installer produces a prefixed static crypto archive and matching authenticated bindgen-generated Rust bindings. BUILD_SHARED_LIBS, BUILD_AWSLC_PROVIDER and ENABLE_CRYPTO_POLICIES remain explicitly OFF; the Linux production crypto source adds no process-spawn, dynamic-loader or locale-conversion call. The dynamic-loading test is excluded and Windows loader calls are outside this Linux scope. Installed source headers, namespace, actual CMake options, generated bindings and linked archive are independently checked and bound into the image receipt. The source LICENSE is SHA256-bound and retains the reviewed composite SPDX obligations. This change does not alter the managed runtime profile, default DTLS path, scope or expiry.
